en: Chan Master Yongming Shou manifested his traces during the Five Dynasties and the early Song period.
Our Emperor Xianzong praised him for his dedicated cultivation of the Pure Land practice and his universal benefit to all sentient beings.
The Emperor of Xī (Xīfēng) bestowed the title Chan Master Miaoyuán Zhèngxiū Zhìjué upon him, designating him as a patriarch of the orthodox lineage of the Buddha-dharma.

His writings, such as the *Zōngjìnglù* (Record of the Mirror of the Source), the *Wànshàn tóngguī jí* (Collection on the Common Return of All Good Deeds), and the *Xīn fù* (Poem on the Mind), have already been included in the Great Canon (*Dàzàng*). Later, Mr.

Huáng Sōngshí of Wǔlín sought out and recovered these scattered works, as well as the master’s poems written during his mountain retreats and the records of his spiritual traces at Yongmíng. Having completed these, he had them carved into printing blocks.
While in Wiyang, I compiled a single volume of my own spiritual records as a manual for the hundred-and-eightfold actual practice of the Master;

it serves as a ferry and raft for those who learn below to reach the heights. I once took it to the capital, but lamented that I had not met with the Great Minister of Justice, Lord Zhang of Yunjian, until too late to present it for inclusion in the imperial canon.
After the Lord passed away, his son, Renzi Bogeing, requested [that I fulfill this].
This has been edited, published, and circulated to support the merit of both the living and the deceased.

May those who read this work revere it with faith and put its teachings into practice, so that every person may obtain the Master’s seal of Amitābha’s tower; this too must surely have been secretly inspired by the spirit of the late Mr.
Gong. This account of the origins was recorded by the layman of Xiyuan, Jiang Gongfei. At that time...
On the first day of the fifth month in the summer of the tenth year of the Qianlong era,
the Record of the Self-Cultivation of Chan Master Zhijue of Huiji Yongming Temple,
compiled by his successor, Daozhe Shan of Dayunfeng Chan Temple at Yongping.
The Śramaṇa Shi Wen-chong, residing at Huan Monastery, respectfully re-edited and compiled [this work].
He reverently contemplates that the ancient sages did not boast of their own abilities, and he reflects upon the former worthies who never displayed their own virtues.

Indeed, the Buddhist scriptures contain teachings on first practicing self-cultivation and then transforming others, while the Confucian tradition marks its principles with the text stating that one should promote the worthy from within without avoiding even close relatives. Thus, the Master has constantly demonstrated...
Tuyu said: While examining the *Hongming ji*, I found that a former virtuous master had a section titled "Examining and Rectifying the Three Karmas," which states:

"When the sentiment of self-reproach is still obscure and the principle of precise discernment has not yet been manifested, one uses external matters to examine and verify the mind; this applies to all that is practiced and cultivated."
Since I know I am incapable [of this], my negligence increases all the more. What is meant by "examination"?

From dawn until noon, from noon until evening, from evening until night, and from night until dawn—even down to a single hour, a single moment, a single thought, or a single instant—how many thoughts, how many mental formations, how many virtues, and how many evils have there been?
How many thoughts have sought to subdue the afflictions (*kleśa*), and how many thoughts...
How many thoughts subdue the enmity of Māra? How many thoughts contemplate the Triple Gem and the Four Noble Truths? How many thoughts realize suffering, emptiness, and impermanence?
How many thoughts contemplate repaying the kindness of one's parents? How many thoughts aspire to undergo suffering on behalf of sentient beings?

How many thoughts resolve upon the bodhisattva path? How many thoughts desire to practice giving and uphold the precepts? How many thoughts desire to practice patience and diligence? How many thoughts desire to practice dhyāna?

Jixianhui: How many thoughts are there that desire to compassionately rescue those in the five realms? How many thoughts are there that desire to exhort and encourage the practice of what is difficult to perform?

How many thoughts are there that desire to transcend and seek the discernment of what is difficult to discern? How many thoughts are there that desire to endure suffering for the sake of establishing the Buddha-dharma?

How many thoughts are there that desire to become a Buddha to transform and deliver all living beings? Having already examined the mind as above, one next examines the speech, starting from the aforementioned time until dawn.

Come. You have already been able to expound several phrases of profound meaning; you have already been able to read and study several scriptures; you have already been able to recite several passages of text;
you have already several times praised the merits of the Buddha; you have already several times extolled the practices of the Bodhisattvas;
you have already several times offered praise and sympathetic joy; and you have already several times dedicated your merit and made vows. Next, examine once more...
Body: Over the course of time mentioned above, how many times have you bowed your body to pay homage to the Buddha? How many times have you bowed your body to pay homage to the Dharma and the Sangha?
How many times have you performed manual labor, such as sweeping stupas and smearing the ground with plaster?
How many times have you burned incense and scattered flowers? How many times have you swept away dust and grime to properly arrange the offerings? How many times have you hung...
Regarding the offering of palms joined before a banner at a stūpa, how many times have you already circumambulated the Buddha with reverence—ten, a hundred, or a thousand times?
Examining it in this way, those who have realized the principle are extremely few, while those who contravene the Way are exceedingly many. Pure and wholesome karma is barely worth mentioning;

heavy afflictions and obstacles fill the eyes like a dense forest. As darkness and obstructions continue to accumulate, by what means can liberation be attained? Having conducted such an examination of oneself...
To save others without merit is impossible; how can one have leisure to discuss the good and evil of others?

Therefore, one must use the three karmas to admonish and examine oneself, knowing how much good and how much evil one has committed. Thus, if one does not first restrain and examine oneself, how can one transform and guide the various capacities of sentient beings?
For this reason, Bodhisattvas, in order to deliver sentient beings, first practice cultivation themselves. As the Vimalakīrti Sūtra says: "The support..."
With immeasurable wealth, he gathers in the poor; with pure observance of the precepts, he gathers in those who violate them; with patience and disciplined conduct, he gathers in those who are angry;
with great diligence, he gathers in those who are indolent; with single-minded meditative concentration, he gathers in those whose minds are distracted;

and with definitive wisdom, he gathers in those who lack knowledge. Furthermore, a sutra says: "One upholds the precepts oneself and encourages others to uphold them; one practices seated meditation oneself..."
He exhorted others to practice seated meditation. The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "Our original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha, did not abandon the merit of threading a needle.
The patriarch Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva explained: "It is like an old man of a hundred years dancing; why is this? It is for the sake of teaching his children and grandchildren.
How much more so for those who have not yet reached the ultimate stage—this is entirely the gate of self-benefit, beginning from the initial mind of the ten stages of faith.

Having passed through the ten abodes (*vihāra*), the ten practices (*caryā*), the ten transferences (*pariṇāmana*), and the ten stages (*bhūmi*), one reaches the stage of Samantabhadra before the Buddha of Equal Enlightenment (*samyaksambuddha*).

This still pertains to the gates of self-benefit and benefiting others; only upon ascending to the stage of Sublime Enlightenment (*suviśuddhabodhi*) and reaching the Samantabhadra following the Buddha does one’s conduct become purely that of benefiting others.

Therefore, after clarifying the causes through these practices and instructions, he then inquires about the conduct to be performed—whether it be taught by a teacher or spoken of spontaneously—and thus it is compiled.
Volume Two and Three. Since my own conduct has become worthy of observation, the gateway of gathering and transforming others shall not fall into ruin.
Because of this benefit, I venture to compose this account. Herein I record in full the one hundred and eight Buddhist rites performed daily between day and night, as detailed below.
First, throughout one's entire life, wherever one may be, one shall constantly construct a Lotus Sutra Hall to adorn the Pure Land.
Second, one shall constantly perform the Lotus Sutra Repentance on behalf of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm during the six periods of every day and night.

Third, constantly cultivate the pure karma of peaceful nourishment (An-yang). Dedicate every atom of goodness, moment by moment, universally for all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm, collectively turning it toward rebirth in that land.

Fourth, at times while practicing seated meditation, he universally aspires that all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm may together enter the wondrous nature of the dharma-illumination of meditative wisdom.

Fifth, every night when ascending the hall to preach the Dharma, he universally intends for the assembly of Chan practitioners and all sentient beings of the dharma-realm in the ten directions to awaken together.
The Sixth: The Sublime Principle of the One Vehicle of the Mind School.

Daily, one should recite one volume of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* in seven fascicles, following each chapter. Above, this is to repay the fourfold profound恩情 (*en*) [of parents, teachers, sovereigns, and the Three Jewels];
below, it is for the sake of all sentient beings within the twenty-five realms of existence throughout the entire Dharma-realm. May they all realize the [Buddha-nature].
Regarding the five kinds of samādhi, manifesting forms throughout the ten realms to transform sentient beings equally and repay the four debts of gratitude:
first, repaying the kindness of teachers and elders for their instruction and guidance; second, repaying the kindness of parents for their nurturing and upbringing.
Third, to repay the kindness of the king who sustained me; fourth, to repay the kindness of the donors who provided for me.
As for those below within the twenty-five realms of existence: first, for the realm of hell, to realize the Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement;

second, for the realm of animals, to realize the Samādhi of Non-retrogression; third, for the realm of hungry ghosts, to realize the Samādhi of Mental Joy; fourth, for the realm of asuras, to realize...
1. The Samādhi of Joy; 2. For Jambudvīpa, the realization of the Illusion-like Samādhi;
3. For Pūrvavideha, the realization of the Sunlight Samādhi; 4. For Aparagoyānī, the realization of the Moonlight Samādhi; 5.
For Uttarakuru, the realization of the Blazing Flame Samādhi; 6. For the Four Heavenly Kings, the realization of the Immovable Samādhi.
10. For the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the realization of the Samādhi Difficult to Subdue. 11. For the Yāma Heaven, the realization of the Samādhi of Examining the Mind.
12. For the Tuṣita Heaven, the realization of the Samādhi of Blue Color. 13.
For the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the realization of the Samādhi of Yellow Color. 14. For the Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven, the realization of the Samādhi of Red Color.
15. He attains the White-Color Samādhi as a realization of the First Dhyāna. 16. He attains the Various Samādhis as a realization of the Brahmā King Heaven.
17. He attains the Twin Samādhi as a realization of the Second Dhyāna. 18. He attains the Thunder-Sound Samādhi as a realization of the Third Dhyāna. 19.
He attains the Torrential Rain Samādhi as a realization of the Fourth Dhyāna. 20. He becomes an Anāgāmin.
Twenty-one is the Samādhi of Realizing Emptiness through the Heaven of No-Thought;
twenty-two is the Samādhi of Realizing Permanence through the Heaven of Infinite Space; twenty-three is the Samādhi of Realizing Bliss through the Heaven of Infinite Consciousness;
twenty-four is the Samādhi of Realizing Self through the Heaven of Nothingness; twenty-five is the Heaven of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception...
He attained the samādhi of the "neither-perception-nor-non-perception" heaven and the threefold purity.
Seventh, he recited the eight fascicles of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-sūtra* every day for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm suffering from the eight kinds of suffering.
Liberation from suffering is the eighth.
Every day, one should read the "Chapter on Pure Conduct" from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* and, according to the text,
make one hundred and forty great vows, so that all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma realm who see or hear them may all enter [into awakening].
The Ninth Path:
Constantly recite the Thousand-Handed, Thousand-Eyed Great Compassionate Dhāraṇī during the six periods of the day and night for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm,
repenting for all obstructions created by the six sense faculties.

Tenth: Constantly recite the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī* with the added verses during the six periods of the day and night for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire *dharmadhātu*, repenting for all transgressions committed by the six sense faculties.

Eleventh: Universally for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm, one takes refuge in and pays homage to the Triple Gem during the six periods of day and night, as well as performing the morning prostrations to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
First, homage to the Jewel of the Buddha:
I bow my head to the Perfectly Omniscient Awakened One, The source of quiescence, equality, and primordial truth;
Adorned with marks and signs, neither existent nor non-existent, His light of wisdom universally illuminates lands as numerous as motes of dust.

With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to all the Buddha-Jewels, the Honored Ones Among Two-Legged Beings, who eternally abide within all lands as numerous as the atoms of the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time;
to the Dharma-Jewels of this realm and other quarters, whether in the human world or the heavens;
and to every true-body relic, image, stupa, and temple. I pray that the majestic spiritual power of the Triple Gem will protect and shield [this place].
There are abodes where various Buddhas dwell; I vow that my individual emanation bodies shall go to each of them to pay homage.

Although I cannot perceive the body that performs the prostration nor the Buddha who is the object of the prostration, yet the illusory appearance remains unimpaired, manifesting as reflections throughout the Dharma-realm.
Second, paying homage to the Dharma Jewel:

I bow my head to the profound, true, and wondrous Dharma— The twelvefold Sūtras, most deep, which are neither text nor letter, And cannot be proclaimed by words; yet in a single sound, All beings understand them according to their own kind.

With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to all the eternally abiding Dharma-treasures within the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space and the pervasive Dharma-realm across the ten directions and three periods of time—the Honored Ones who have transcended desire, the twelve divisions of the scriptures, and all sacred texts hidden in the palaces of devas, humans, dragons, and the oceans.
As before, when prostrating to the Buddhas, direct the mind toward every location where these scriptural volumes reside. One.
With one part of my body, I go everywhere to pay homage.
I prostrate three times before the Sangha Jewel,
bowing my head to the pure and holy sages— the harmonious Arhats of the ten directions.
Upholding the prohibitive precepts without transgression, shaking the mendicant’s staff and carrying the water jar for the benefit of sentient beings,

I single-mindedly pay respectful homage to the Sangha Jewel— the Honored Among All— dwelling eternally within all lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm across the ten directions and three periods of time;
to those great [beings] in precious lands, pure realms, mountain caves, and stone chambers.
The Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and all the worthy sages likewise prostrate to the Buddha as before.
They direct their minds toward every place where the Saṃgha resides, and with each individual emanation, they go there to pay homage.
Next, holding the incense burner, one says: "I reverently offer incense and flowers according to the Dharma.

May these clouds of incense and flowers become a radiant platform to make offerings to all Buddhas, the Sutras and Dharmas, all Bodhisattvas, the assembly of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, as well as all celestial beings and immortals.
May they accept them and perform Buddha-works. I universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm shall all enter [the Way]."
I make offerings within the ocean of the Dharma-realm, together realizing the single, true realm of non-arising.

With a single mind, I hold aloft the incense burner and contemplate these fragrant fumes as they transform into pearls, necklaces, incense altars, jeweled towers, celestial robes, exquisite music, wondrous fruits, clouds of flowers, and all manner of ritual implements.
I offer these to the Buddhas of the ten directions, performing great Buddha-works.
I pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I pay respectful homage to the Buddha Virtue of Goodness in the eastern direction, and to all Buddhas throughout the entire dharma-realm of the east.

With single-minded devotion, I pay respectful homage to the Buddha Virtue of Freedom from Sorrow in the southeastern direction, and to all [Buddhas] throughout the entire dharma-realm of the southeast.
To all Buddhas:
with single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Buddha Candanagandha in the southern direction, and to all Buddhas throughout the entire dharma-realm of the south.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Buddha Ratnadatta in the southwestern direction, and to all Buddhas throughout the entire dharma-realm of the southwest.
Buddha, with single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Buddha Amitābha of the western direction and to all Buddhas throughout the entire dharma-realm of the west.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Buddha Padmaśrī of the northwest direction and to all [Buddhas] throughout the entire dharma-realm of the northwest.
Buddha. With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Buddha Lakṣaṇaguṇa in the northern direction, and to all Buddhas throughout the entire dharma-realm of the north.
With single-minded reverence, I pay homage to the Buddha Triyānacara in the northeastern direction, and to all [Buddhas] throughout the entire dharma-realm of the northeast.
To all Buddhas,
I single-mindedly pay respectful homage to the Buddha Universal Array of Vast Virtues in the upper direction, and to all Buddhas throughout the entirety of the dharma-realm in the upper direction.
With a single mind, I pay respectful homage to the Buddha of Luminous Virtue in the lower direction, and to all Buddhas throughout the entirety of the dharma-realm in the lower direction.
Twelfth: Every day, universally for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, prostrate before the precious stūpa containing the true-body relics of Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
May transgressions be extinguished and merit arise; may obstacles be eliminated and the Way be manifested.

Thirteenth: I have personally composed the "Text of Six Hundred Vows of Mahāyāna Compassion and Wisdom. Every day, I universally make these vows and perform prostrations on behalf of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma realm.
Fourteenth: At dawn, pay homage to the Upādhyāya and the Honored Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha on Vulture Peak Mountain.
May all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm universally succeed in upholding and flourishing the Triple Gem.
Fifteenth: At dawn, pay homage to the True, Pure, and Sublime Dharma of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
Universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm may together realize the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Samādhi* and be born together in the pure land of Amitābha.
Sixteenth: At dawn, pay homage to the Ācārya Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of Great Wisdom in the Golden World (*Suvarṇabhadrāloka*).
May all sentient beings throughout the entire *dharmadhātu* enter the gateway of the *dharmadhātu* and open the fundamental wisdom (*mūlaprajñā*).

Seventeenth: At dawn, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, one should walk while bearing Amitābha Buddha upon the crown of one’s head, relying upon the power of his vast vows and aspiring toward the perfect cultivation of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Eighteenth: At dawn, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate while reciting the One-Syllable King Heart Dharani.
May all universally vow to perfectly realize the heart-king and abide in the station of total retention (*dhāraṇī*). The mantra is:
Oṃ bulim-phe.

Nineteenth: At dawn, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate while recollecting Śākyamuni Buddha, vowing to succeed the Benevolent One and achieve the patience of quiescent extinction.

Twenty: At dawn, universally for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, circumambulate and recite the name of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, vowing to accomplish the wondrous wisdom of non-substantiality and become a son of the Dharma King.
Twenty-first. At noon. I pay homage and take refuge in Amitābha Buddha of the Land of Peace and Bliss.
May all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma realm suddenly awaken to their own minds and realize the wondrous Pure Land.
The twenty-second [session]. At noon: I pay homage to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Inconceivable Treasury of the Buddha.
May all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm universally aspire to enter the gate of the nature-virtue of dependent origination and roam within the ocean of Vairocana’s great vows.
Twenty-third. At the hour of the horse (noon). I pay homage and repent before the Great Practitioner Samantabhadra Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva of the Silver-Colored World.
I universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may realize the emptiness of the nature of offenses and accomplish the Repentance of Non-arising.
Twenty-fourth. At the hour of the horse (midday). For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate while reciting the original mantra of Avalokiteśvara.
May they universally attain the body of universal penetration and accomplish the practice of the Universal Gate.
The mantra is: Oṃ sīlavibhāni svāhā.
Twenty-fifth. At the hour of the horse (noon). For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm, circumambulate while reciting the name of Prabhūtaratna Buddha.
May his manifested bodies disperse their forms so that we may together realize the One Vehicle.
Twenty-sixth. At the hour of the horse (midday). For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate while recollecting Samantabhadra Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
May there be the fulfillment of the gateways of diverse wisdom and the mobilization of wondrous practices that have no beginning or end.

Twenty-seventh. At noon, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, one should practice the path while wearing [the image of] Avalokiteśvara upon the crown of the head, thereby realizing the body of the ultimate reality (bhūtakoṭi) of Avalokiteśvara and manifesting the conduct of great compassion that is identical in essence with all beings.
Twenty-eighth. At dusk, one pays homage to the Master of Instruction and to the Venerable Maitreya Buddha, who is destined to descend from the Tuṣita Heaven.
May all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm universally attain peerless, true compassion and succeed him as the Regent who shall fill the seat of Buddhahood in his next life.
The Twenty-ninth. At dusk, I pay homage to the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, the treasury of the pure Dharma.

I universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the entire *dharmadhātu* may practice the skillful means of non-apprehension and perfect the circular gateway of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).

The Thirtieth [Observance]: At dusk, one pays homage to the fellow practitioner and dharma-companion, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara of Great Compassion who Relieves Suffering on Mount Potalaka, and to all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm.
One universally prays that all sentient beings in the Dharma-realm may enter the Gate of Perfect Penetration and carry out practices that encompass the Dharma-realm.
Thirty-first: At twilight, universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma realm circumambulate while reciting the Manjuśrī-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī.
Universally pray that they enter the gateway of the letter A and realize the nature of non-arising.
The mantra is: *A ra pa ca na*.

Thirty-second: At twilight, universally for all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, circumambulate while recollecting the emanation-buddhas of Śākyamuni, making the vow that they shall extensively spread clouds of bodies and enter into the signs of attaining enlightenment.

Thirty-third: At twilight, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma realm, circumambulate and contemplate Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, who is endowed with the fourteen fearlessnesses; may he bestow blessings and protection upon all sentient beings.

Thirty-fourth: At dusk, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm, one shall carry the precious stupa of Śākyamuni upon the crown of the head while walking the path, universally for the purpose of perpetuating the lineage of the Buddhas and eternally serving as a field of merit for the Dharma-realm.

Thirty-fifth. At the beginning of the night, one pays homage to the witness-teacher: the past Buddha Prabhūtaratna within the stupa of the seven treasures, and all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
May all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm, in accordance with their original vows, assist in turning the wheel of the Dharma.
The thirty-sixth. At the beginning of the first watch of the night, I pay homage to the *Tathatā-samudra-kośa* (Treasury of the Ocean of True Suchness) of the *Mahāratnakūṭa Sūtra*.
I universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm may rely upon sūtras of definitive meaning and penetrate the wondrous intent of the Buddha.

Thirty-seventh. At the beginning of the night, I pay homage to the Compassionate Teacher, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta of the World of Peace and Bliss, and to the entire ocean-like assembly of pure beings.
May all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm universally fulfill their aspirations.
To guide and benefit sentient beings, may we together realize that the pure land is mind-only.
(38) At the first watch of the night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate while reciting the Heart Dharani of Avalokiteśvara of the Lotus Family.
May all universally aspire to possess the gate of great compassion and perfect sovereign wisdom. The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ alu le ke svāhā. (39) At the first watch of the night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate and recite the name of the Compassionate Honored One Maitreya Buddha.
May they be born in the Inner Court and personally realize the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*).
Fortieth: During the first watch of the night, universally for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, circumambulate while recollecting the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
May they restrain their faculties, maintain pure mindfulness in succession, and take rebirth upon the lotus pedestal.
Forty-first. During the first watch of the night, he universally bore the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* upon his head for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm;
practicing the Way, he fully entered the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi* and together returned to the ultimate One Vehicle.
Forty-second. At midnight, one pays homage to the Śākyamuni Buddhas who are emanations throughout the ten directions.
One universally prays that all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, without leaving their seats of enlightenment, may manifest a hundred billion emanations.
Forty-third: At midnight, I pay homage to the secret treasury of all Buddhas in the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra.
I universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm may clarify their own intrinsic nature-mind and abide in the secret treasury.
Forty-fourth. At midnight, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, the Greatly Compassionate Savior from Suffering.
I universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may realize the stainless samādhi and deliver those in the evil realms.
Forty-fifth. At midnight, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate while reciting the *Suvarṇacakravarti-uṣṇīṣa-dhāraṇī*.
May all universally aspire that the Unseen Uṣṇīṣa (Anavalokitamūrdha) becomes a Wheel-Turning King (*cakravartin*). The mantra is:
Oṃ daḷiṃ.

Forty-sixth: At midnight, universally for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, circumambulate while reciting the name of the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light Buddha, vowing that his original vows become like a wind-wheel to enable rebirth in the precious land.
Forty-seventh: At midnight, universally for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, circumambulate while recollecting the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, making this vow:
"May you act as the Great King of Physicians to rescue and deliver all."

Forty-eighth. At midnight, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm, he bore the Avataṃsaka Sūtra upon his head and practiced the Way, whereby they all entered the Sea-Seal Samādhi and suddenly awakened to the Perfect Doctrine of the Dharma-realm.
Forty-ninth: During the final watch of the night, pay homage to the Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha of the Eastern World-realm of the Full Moon.
May all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm universally resolve to give rise to the great vow-mind and gather in boundless multitudes.
Fiftieth: During the final watch of the night, one pays homage to the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-sūtra*, the profound scripture of non-arising.
For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire *dharmadhātu*, one secretly unites with the true mind and realizes that there is nothing to be attained.

Fifty-first: During the final watch of the night, pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja. May it be universally prayed that for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, the medicine of the sublime Dharma be proclaimed to eliminate the disease of afflictions.

Fifty-second: During the final watch of the night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate while reciting the Heart-to-Heart Dharani of the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
May all universally aspire to realize the adamantine samādhi and the firm body of a Buddha.
The mantra is: Oṃ ulenī svāhā.

Fifty-third: During the final watch of the night, universally for all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, circumambulate while reciting the name of Amitābha Buddha, vowing to achieve supreme wisdom and to gather and transform sentient beings.

Fifty-fourth. During the final watch of the night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, I shall carry the Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra upon my head and practice its path, vowing to enter the gate of non-abiding contemplation and achieve the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).

Fifty-fifth. During the final watch of the night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, circumambulate while recollecting the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, making this vow:
"May you spread your unconditioned compassion and deliver us from the sufferings of the three miserable realms."

Fifty-sixth: Whenever there is a moment of leisure, while circumambulating and practicing the Way, I universally pray that all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma realm may attain a body of purple-gold light, with the marks and signs of perfection fully complete.
Fifty-seventh: To read and recite Mahāyāna sūtras, universally aspiring that all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm may together clarify the Buddha-wisdom.
Fifty-eighth: During the six periods of day and night, to universally recollect the seven Tathāgatas for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm.
Recite the name of the Tathāgata Ratnavijaya: may all sentient beings purify all the afflictions accumulated throughout kalpas of dust and toil.
Recite the name of the Tathāgata Vigatabhaya: may all sentient beings be free from the five fears and attain the bliss of nirvana.
Recite the name of the Tathāgata Vipulakāya: may the throats of all sentient beings become vast, and may they be filled with the joy of dhyāna.
Sufficient. Recite the name of the Tathāgata King of Ambrosia: may all sentient beings drink the flavor of ambrosia and attain great bodhi.
Recite the name of the Tathāgata Wondrous Form Body: may all sentient beings be free from ugly forms and be endowed with the perfection of the marks and signs.
Recite the name of the Tathāgata Many Treasures: may all sentient beings forever leave poverty behind and be fully possessed of the wealth of the Dharma.
Recite the name of Amitābha Tathāgata, vowing that all sentient beings may leave behind the forms of the evil realms and that their spirits may dwell in the Pure Land.
(Fifty-ninth) At dawn, universally for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, uphold the six mindfulnesses of the Mahāyāna.
1. Mindfulness of the Buddha: wishing to attain the body of a Buddha. 2. Mindfulness of the Dharma: wishing to turn the wheel of the Dharma.

3. Mindfulness of the Sangha: wishing to provide protection and refuge for the assembly. 4. Mindfulness of the Precepts: wishing to fulfill all vows. 5. Mindfulness of Generosity: relinquishing all afflictions. 6. Mindfulness of the Devas.
Desiring to fulfill the All-Knowledge of the God among Gods, [this is] the sixtieth [chapter].

Six times throughout the day and night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm of the ten directions, one burns incense toward each direction to make offerings to the Triple Gem of the ten directions. May this incense transform into precious jewels, necklaces, and towers.
Sixty-first: With jeweled towers, music, flowers, fruits, clothing, food, drink, and various kinds of offering implements, one makes offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Throughout the six periods of day and night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, one takes refuge in the Ten Directions.
I take refuge in the Three Jewels. May all beings enter the noble stages of the three vehicles and realize the Dharma-body of five aspects.
(62) Throughout the six periods of day and night, I universally praise the Three Jewels for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm of the ten directions.
May I possess the Brahma-voice and the foremost of physical forms.
(63) At dawn, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, may I generate the bodhicitta on their behalf;
and may I vow that in every thought-moment, supreme bodhi shall be perfected, continuing without interruption until the final moment of mind. May I generate the bodhicitta.

Mind. The mantra is: Oṃ maitrī-mudrapāṇaye mi. (64) During the six periods of day and night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, scatter flowers as an offering to the Triple Gem in the ten directions.
May these flowers fill the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, performing great Buddha-works and causing [all beings] to...
May all sentient beings obtain the adornment and purity of the environmental retribution, and may they always dwell in wondrous lands scattering flowers.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvatathāgata-puṣpa-maṇi hūṃ hūṃ.
Sixty-fifth. At dawn, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, hold aloft the incense burner and burn incense.
Repent of past karma and recite the *Dhāraṇī for the Extinction of Sins of the Seven Buddhas*.
Universally vow that the three karmas be without artifice and ultimately pure. The mantra is as follows: *Līpā līpā-ti, ghu-gu-ti, dhāraṇī-ti, ni*.
Hara-ti pi-li-ni-ti ma-ha-ka-ti chen-ling gan-ti sa-ha.
(66) At dawn, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm in the ten directions, I bestow the Bodhisattva precepts.
May they, by virtue of the majestic spiritual power of the Triple Gem, appear one by one before me, so that all may receive them directly.

Sixty-seventh. At dawn, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, one should contemplate the *Dhāraṇī of Giving and Precepts*, universally wishing that they may be fully endowed with the Buddha’s discipline, remaining pure and without transgression.
The mantra is: *Sara pratijñākṣa hili dhaye svāhā*.

Sixty-eighth. At the hour of the horse (noon). For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, I hold aloft the incense burner and burn incense, reciting the Heart-and-Mind Mantra of the Buddhas.
May all universally aspire to give rise to the true and wondrous mind and open the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ maṇidāri hūṃ phaṭ. (69) At twilight, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, hold aloft the incense burner and burn incense while reciting the Heart Mantra of Amitābha Buddha.
May they all realize the Buddha-mind and be reborn together in Sukhāvatī. The mantra:
It is said: Oṃ amṛtatejohara hūṃ. (Seventieth.
At the first watch of the night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, hold aloft the incense burner, burn incense, and recite the Prajñā-mahākaruṇā-citta-dhāraṇī.
May all beings sincerely realize their own minds and the perfect luminosity of prajñā. The mantra is as follows:
Tadyathā gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā. (71) At midnight,
for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, hold up the incense burner, burn incense, and recite this seven times.
The Great Dhāraṇī of the Mantra of Cundī, Mother of Ten Million Buddhas. May all beings find rest within the womb of the Dharma-realm and conceive the seed of Bodhi. The mantra says:
I bow my head in refuge to Susiddhi; I prostrate with my crown to the seven koṭis.
I now praise this great dhāraṇī; May you, out of compassion, grant your protection. Namo sabhūtānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhakoti-nāṃ tadyathā oṃ cale cule cuṭe saṃva...
(2) Ha. Seventy-second.

During the final watch of the night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, hold aloft the incense burner and burn incense while reciting the *A* syllable, the Dharani of the Wisdom-Mind Door of All Buddhas.
May they all enter the gate of non-arising and be endowed with the true Buddha.
Wisdom. The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām ā*.

(73) During the six periods of day and night, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, one should receive and maintain the vajra-bell, vajra-pestle, and *vajra* [implements].
First, empower the bell and pestle with the following mantra: *Oṃ vajra...*
*Rāgaṇḍa-hūṃ*. Next, ring the bell to awaken all Tathāgatas throughout the entire realm of empty space. The mantra is:
*Oṃ vajra-krodha*. Next, ring this bell pervading the entire Dharma-realm to perform great Buddha-deeds, awakening all ignorant ordinary beings.
May they all, upon hearing the sound of the bell, awaken to the Mahā...
The Prajñāpāramitā. Seventy-fourth.
Six times throughout the day and night, one practices the five repentances and purifies the six sense faculties.

Universally for the sake of all within the Dharma-realm—the four debts of gratitude, the twenty-five states of existence, and the twelve classes of beings—one relies upon the power of the Triple Gem and, facing the ten directions...
Before the Buddha, with a sincere heart, we repent for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm:

from the beginningless past when they possessed spirit and consciousness until this very day, they have, due to ignorance, falsely created all cycles of birth and death, following along with circumstances that are either adverse or favorable.
They give rise to hearts of love and hatred; they stir the six sense faculties; they commit sins as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Since many kalpas past, because the faculty of the eye has been greedily attached to forms through causes and conditions, they have craved all sensory objects.

Because they receive these objects, wherever they are born in this human body, they may become attached to various forms. When forms destroy their eyes, they become slaves to affection and craving; thus, forms cause them to wander.
Transmigrating through the three realms, I have been driven by these defilements; blind and without vision, my faculty of sight was unwholesome, causing me much injury.
Although the Buddhas of the ten directions are eternally present and never extinguished, I did not see them because my eyes were obscured by turbid evil.
Now I have finally awakened and shall recite and uphold the Mahāyāna Inconceivable Treasury. I take refuge in Samantabhadra and all the World-Honored Ones, and grant that I...
Together with all the grave offenses committed by the faculty of the eye of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, may they be ultimately purified.
I now repent for the faculty of the ear: from time immemorial, due to the causes and conditions of the ear-faculty, it has followed after external sounds;

when hearing sublime sounds, the mind gives rise to delusion and attachment; when hearing harsh sounds, it arouses the one hundred and eight kinds of afflictions that act as thieves and bring harm. Thus it is.
Having evil ears, they receive retribution in the form of misfortune and constantly hear evil sounds.

Because they give rise to various攀緣 (pān-yuán, objects of attachment) through perverted listening, they fall into the evil realms and borderlands where they do not hear the True Dharma; they are deluded and attached everywhere, with no moment’s rest.
Sitting amidst these hollow sounds, my consciousness is wearied. The Buddhas of the ten directions are constantly preaching the Dharma;
it is only because my ears are obstructed by turbid evil that I do not hear it. Now I have finally awakened and shall recite and uphold this Ocean-Treasury of Merit of the Mahāyāna.
I take refuge in Samantabhadra and all World-Honored Ones, so that for myself and all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, all that is produced by the faculty of hearing—
These are grave offenses. Ultimately pure, one should repent for the faculty of the nose.
Since beginningless time, we have been bound by this faculty of the nose; hearing various fragrances, we were deluded and lacked clarity.
All those who were lying down—the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*), the various afflictions (*kleśa*), and the thieves—have now arisen. Because of this discrimination, we fall.

Throughout birth and death, the sublime fragrance of the merits of the Buddhas of the ten directions fills the Dharma-realm; yet because of the turbid and evil obstruction of my nose, I did not perceive it.
Now I have finally awakened to this and recite and uphold the pure and wondrous treasury of the Mahāyāna.

I take refuge in Samantabhadra and all World-Honored Ones, so that all grave offenses committed by the olfactory faculty of myself and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may be extinguished.

Ultimately pure, I repent of the faculty of the tongue. From beginningless time, regarding the unwholesome and evil karma created by the faculty of the tongue— such as being greedily attached to delicious flavors,

harming sentient beings, violating the various prohibitions and precepts, opening the gate of negligence, and furthermore, giving rise to verbal [karma] through the faculty of the tongue— I now repent.
Transgressions and offenses—false speech, frivolous talk, double-tongued speech, and harsh words;

slandering the Triple Gem, praising false views, teaching what is not the Dharma as the Dharma, and teaching the Dharma as what is not the Dharma—all such thorns of evil karma emerge from the faculty of the tongue and sever the Wheel of the True Dharma.
It arises from the faculty of the tongue. Because of these causes and conditions, one shall fall into the evil realms for hundreds of kalpas and thousands of lifetimes, with no time of escape.
The flavor of the Buddhas' Dharma fills the entire Dharma-realm; yet because my defiled and evil tongue acts as an obstruction, I am unable to preach the Dharma.
Now, having begun to awaken, I recite and uphold the secret treasury of all Buddhas of the Mahāyāna. I take refuge in Samantabhadra and all World-Honored Ones,
so that all grave offenses committed by the faculty of the tongue— both my own and those of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm—
may be ultimately purified.

I repent of the faculty of the body. Since beginningless time, this bodily faculty has been unwholesome, greedily attached to various tactile objects, inverted and lacking understanding, with afflictions blazing intensely, giving rise to the three unwholesome acts—namely, killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct—and forming great enmities with all sentient beings;
even to the point of destroying stupas and monasteries, burning scriptures and images, and misappropriating the property of the Triple Gem, without any sense of shame.
Shameful! Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless; arising from the actions of the body, they could never be fully recounted.
The Buddhas of the ten directions constantly emit pure light that illuminates all things, yet because my own body is defiled and evil, I am obstructed and do not perceive it.

I know only how to crave and cling to coarse, wretched, and foul tactile sensations, thereby undergoing manifold sufferings in the present, and subsequently suffering in the realms of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts.
Immersed within such various sufferings, I was neither aware nor conscious of them; only now do I awaken.

Reciting and upholding the true Dharma-treasury of the Mahāyāna, I take refuge in Samantabhadra and all World-Honored Ones, so that all grave offenses committed by the physical faculties of myself and all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm may be ultimately purified.
I repent of the faculty of mind (*manas*). Since beginningless time, this faculty of mind has been unwholesome, greedily attached to all phenomena, and deluded by ignorance, failing to understand.
Following after objects of perception, it gives rise to greed, anger, and delusion; there is no among the eight heterodoxies or the eight difficulties that one has not experienced.
Such a faculty of mind is the very root of all birth and death and the source of all suffering. As it is said in the sutras: [Exegesis].
Kāśyapa, he is named Vairocana, pervading all places. You should know that all phenomena are themselves the Buddha-dharma.
Through deluded conceptualization, one undergoes various torments; this is to perceive impurity within awakening and to bind oneself within liberation.
Now, for the first time, you have awakened and recite and uphold the Mahāyāna perfection.
Fulfilling the treasury of Dharma, I take refuge in Samantabhadra and all World-Honored Ones.

May I sever the continuity of all grave offenses committed by the mental faculties of sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, as well as the immeasurable and boundless karmic obstacles of evil deeds arising from the six sense organs—
whether already committed, currently being committed, or yet to be committed in the future— and may I attain ultimate purity.

Purity. Seventy-fifth. During the six periods of day and night, together with all sentient beings of the entire dharma-realm, one should exhort all Buddhas of the ten directions to manifest in the world, to constantly turn the wheel of Dharma, and—should they be about to enter parinirvāṇa—to remain for a long time.
Abiding thus, throughout the realm of sentient beings, may they all emerge from the wheel of suffering and reach their original mind, returning together to the ocean of purity.

(Seventy-sixth. During the six periods of day and night, together with all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, I rejoice in the inexhaustible merit of the Buddhas of the ten directions and the great Bodhisattvas, as well as in the actions performed by all ordinary beings, both those with outflows and...
All untainted and subtle roots of goodness without exception enter the perfect cause, together realizing the Wisdom of All Modes (Sarvākārajñatā).
[This is] the seventy-seventh [vow]. During the six periods of day and night, one dedicates these together with all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm.
From beginningless time until this very day, whatever has been performed by the three karmas—even a single thought-moment of a root of goodness—is entirely used for universal bestowal upon all.
Dedicate all sentient beings of the entire dharma-realm toward unsurpassed bodhi, so that they may together be reborn in the pure land of the West.
(Seventy-eighth. During the six periods of day and night, together with all sentient beings of the entire dharma-realm, make this vow:
may all sentient beings of the entire dharma-realm personally realize the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi* and suddenly awaken to the perfect fulfillment of the One Vehicle. At the moment of death...

At the time of death, their consciousness shall remain undisturbed; defiled karma will be extinguished, and right mindfulness will manifest before them. They shall be reborn in the Western Pure Land according to their vows.

Taking refuge in Amitābha Buddha, they shall achieve the mind of great patience, enter universally throughout the Dharma-realm, and until the end of the future, protect and uphold the treasury of the True Dharma.
They shall expound the gateway of the One Vehicle and bring the Bodhi of the Buddhas to full completion.

I shall cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra, as vast as the Dharma-realm and as ultimate as space; I vow that together with all sentient beings, we shall simultaneously attain the Way of Buddhahood.

Seventy-ninth: Every day, on behalf of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, at the six periods of the day and night, with single-minded devotion burn incense and take refuge in the Heavenly King.
Establish a separate site for practice and offer worship for as long as you live, relying upon the majestic radiance of the Bodhisattva.
Peacefully treading the Way.

Number Eighty. Every day, on behalf of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, at the six periods of day and night, one should recollect the Heart Mantra of the Heavenly King. The mantra is: Oṃ siriye svāhā.

Eighty-first. Every day, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, recite the *Tianwang hushen zhenyan* (Mantra for the Heavenly King’s Protection of the Body) during the six periods of the day and night.
May all sentient beings have peace in body and flourish in the Way, forever eliminating the afflictions of Māra.
The mantra is: Oṃ yakṣa-vajra svāhā.

Eighty-second. For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, one should separately establish a site of practice (bodhimaṇḍa) during the six periods of day and night to make offerings to Prajñā and recite the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
One should also chant and contemplate the Name, vowing that all sentient beings may, by relying on this dharma-gate of great majestic power, manifest the wisdom of the Buddhas of the ten directions.

Eighty-third: For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, one should separately establish a site of practice (bodhimaṇḍa) during the six periods of day and night to make offerings to the honored image of Avalokiteśvara.
One should circumambulate it during these six periods and recite the sacred name, vowing that all sentient beings may perfect the five eyes and manifest the ten bodies.

Eighty-fourth: For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, one should separately arrange incense and flowers during the six periods of day and night to make offerings to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, so that they may together awaken to the ultimate One Vehicle and all realize the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Samādhi*.

Eighty-fifth: Every night, he universally offers food and water to all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, as well as to all hungry ghosts of the wilderness and all starving beings who travel by water, on land, or through the air.
Eighty-sixth: Every night, one should constantly bestow the Three Refuges according to the Dharma upon the spirits and ghosts of the nine grades and all sentient beings of the dharma realm.
Eighty-seventh:
Every night, one should constantly bestow the Samaya precepts upon all spirits and ghosts, as well as the officials of the underworld of the six realms.
The mantra is: Oṃ samayas tvaṃ (pronounced *pūjin*). Eighty-eighth.
Every night, one should constantly preach the Dharma of the Three Vehicles for all spirits and deities, and for all sentient beings within the dharma-realm.

Eighty-ninth: Receiving and upholding the Ucchuṣma-dhāraṇī. It is universally prayed that for all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, in whatever place they go, may their physical and mental states, as well as all internal and external environments, be entirely pure.
The mantra is: Oṃ buddhajihvākuñcitavimalamahāprahāṇa-huṃ-jik-jik-he-maṇi.
Mī gu ji mī mó nā qī ōng zhé jí nà wū shēn mù jū yì héng héng hūn pàn pàn pàn pàn pàn sā hē.
Ninety: During the six periods of day and night, one should receive and uphold the Inner and Outer Fivefold Offering Dharani.

May all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm—both their internal and external mental states and the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena—become complete implements of offering.
May they offer to immeasurable Tathāgatas, reaching everywhere throughout the ten directions, and perform great Buddha-works. The mantra is: Oṃ Sali...
Vataṃtasatā dūpa puṣpeppe akamale pucchaṃge samudra samudra samaye svāhā.
Ninety-first: The Mantra for Receiving, Upholding, and Dedication. 1. Dedicate to the True Suchness (Tathatā) and the Limit of Reality (Bhūtakoṭi), so that heart and mind are in perfect accord.
2. Dedicate to unsurpassed Bodhi, so that every thought-moment is perfected. 3.
Dedicate to all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, so that they may together be born in the Pure Land. The mantra is: Oṃ samara-vīra-ma-sara-ma.
HA KṢA KĀ RA VA HŪṂ. Ninety-second.

This is the mantra for receiving and maintaining rebirth. I vow that at the time of my final passing, I shall be reborn together with all sentient beings of the entire dharma realm in the Pure Land. Recite this rebirth mantra once.

Ninety-third. Universally for all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, may they uphold this Great Jewel-Birth Empowerment Dhāraṇī of all Tathāgatas, and may it be their firm vow to attain supreme bodhi and become true sons of the Dharma-King. The mantra is: Oṃ sarvatathāgatani-mala-sambhava.
Vai Hūṃ Hūṃ. Ninety-fourth.
During the six periods of day and night, strike the bell universally for all sentient beings throughout the entire *dharmadhātu*. First, one should make this vow:
"May the sound of this bell pervade the *dharmadhātu* and perform great Buddha-works, respectfully inviting all ordinary and holy beings of the ten directions."
The fourfold assembly, each maintaining their proper deportment, followed the procession. Next, they made this vow:
"May the sound of these bells pervade the entire Dharma-realm, awakening all beings in the long night of birth and death, so that all may attain clarity and awareness. Afterwards, they made this vow:

"May the sound of these bells pervade the entire Dharma-realm; universally may all sentient beings suffering in the three miserable realms and the eight difficult conditions hear this and be liberated."
Furthermore, write the *Diyu pozhuan zhenyan* (Mantra for Breaking the Hell Realms). Within it, recite three times orally with the wish:

"May all hells be broken and the gates to the evil destinies be closed. May the sound pervade the ten directions so that all sentient beings suffering there, upon hearing this bell sound, shall all attain liberation.
The *Diyu pozhuan zhenyan* is as follows: *Namo āśatāśvatebhyaḥ samyaksam...*
*Buddha-koṭi-nam-jāra-vāra-sasti-ri-ti-ri svāhā.* (95) At the six periods of day and night,
for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, one should receive and uphold this staff.

I pray that you vibrate this sound of the *khakkhara* throughout the entire Dharma-realm, performing great Buddha-works to awaken all sentient beings in the hells so they may leave suffering behind and attain liberation;
to awaken all sentient beings who suffer from hunger and thirst so that sweet springs shall flow from their mouths;
and to awaken all insects and beasts so that they may all find the way to avoid [the danger], take refuge, and attain liberation.

Ninety-sixth: Constantly gathering fresh flowers to make offerings to all honored images, universally for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, their roots of goodness become supple and they achieve wondrous perfection.
Ninety-seventh: Constantly exhort all people to mind Amitābha Buddha, and through the cultivation of pure karma as well as the two adornments of merit and wisdom—
practicing the precepts, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and cultivating the myriad practices of the six pāramitās—
and even extensively organizing fragrant flower assemblies and pure gatherings to offer great vegetarian feasts and perform various acts of giving, always having a leader to guide them.
Ninety-eighth: He constantly bestows the Bodhisattva precepts upon the fourfold assembly. Ninety-ninth:

He constantly prints and distributes throughout the world images of Amitābha Buddha, as well as the Prajñāpāramitā, Ratnakūṭa, *Śūraṅgama*, and *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* sūtras, along with various divine mantras;
he exhorts others to receive and uphold these ten types of teachings and to make offerings through the three karmas of body, speech, and mind.

One hundred and third: Beyond these three dependencies, one should give away all wealth and possessions at every opportunity to perform conditioned meritorious deeds, to relieve the suffering of the poor, and to make offerings to sentient beings;
one should always release all living beings and cover all sentient beings with compassion.

111. Whenever conditions arise, I shall extensively bestow medicine. May I, throughout the limits of the future, always act as a King of Physicians, universally rescuing all sentient beings from the grave illnesses of body and mind.
102. Constantly wear and carry the Great Uṣṇīṣa [Dhāraṇī], universally wishing that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may forever eliminate demonic obstacles.
103. Constantly wear and carry the hundred inconceivable divine mantras, such as the Mahāpratisarā and others.
May all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm have their aspirations fulfilled as they wish.
(104) Constantly making various offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, water, banners, and canopies at the site of enlightenment, one should perform the Buddha-activities with meticulous solemnity.

Fifteenth: Constantly make offerings to the two fields of compassion and respect. Whether it be water used for rinsing bowls or even a single spittle, offer it all to sentient beings who are hungry ghosts;
or give a single morsel of food to animals, causing them all to resolve upon the unsurpassed mind of bodhicitta.
106. Constantly burn incense as an offering to the *saṃghāṭī* (great robe). Whenever you don it, always make this vow:
"May all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm always wear the unsurpassed field of merit robe of the Tathāgata, and may they be fully endowed with the subtle precepts of the Tathāgata."
170. Whenever receiving porridge or rice, one should always make this vow: first to make offerings to the Three Jewels, who are of one essence throughout the Dharma-realm;
to perform great Buddha-work pervading the entirety of the sand-grained worlds; to cause the donors of the ten directions to fulfill the six perfections;

and to ensure that all hungry and thirsty sentient beings are fully satisfied with the joy of the Dharma. To heal the wounds of hunger, one shall cultivate the pure karma of the Western Paradise until its fulfillment.
For the sake of unsurpassed bodhi, I accept this food. Now, this food shall not nourish the body of saṃsāra, but only the Dharma-body of the fruit of Buddhahood.

May concentration and wisdom now increase. At the time of giving to beings, may it be bestowed universally upon all sentient beings of the six realms, so that they may be fully endowed with the six pāramitās.

The above summarizes the one hundred and eight Buddhist practices performed daily. Herein, the vehicle and the precepts are pursued with equal urgency; the provisional and the ultimate are practiced in tandem;

essence and function mutually encompass one another; and principle and phenomena are without obstruction. Now, I cite the concluding verse from the *Wanshan tonggui ji* (The Collection on the Convergence of Myriad Good Deeds): "By practicing even a single good deed, one attains the Way; How much more so for those who cultivate myriad virtues! If one does not practice this dharma, One will surely fall into the three miserable realms."
To manifest perfect cultivation, the verse says:
Enlightenment is unarisen yet arises; The Buddha-way is unsought yet sought;
Sublime practice is non-practice yet practiced; True wisdom is unconditioned yet acts.
Arousing compassion, one realizes our shared essence; practicing loving-kindness, one enters deeply into the unconditioned.
Giving without anything to relinquish, one practices generosity; observing precepts without grasping, one cultivates concentration and wisdom without anything arising.
Through the practice of patience, one penetrates the state where there is no injury.
Through Prajñā, one awakens to the realm of non-arising; through Samādhi, one knows that the mind abides nowhere.
Reflecting on the formless while possessing form, one realizes the ineffable yet speaks with eloquence.
Establishing a water-moon meditation hall, one adorns the world of intrinsic emptiness.
Arranging offerings of illusory flowers, I make offerings to the Tathāgata who is like a reflection;
I repent that the nature of sin is fundamentally empty. I entreat the Dharmakāya to abide eternally;
I dedicate with the realization that there is nothing to be attained; I rejoice in merits equal to True Suchness (Tathatā).
Praising that which is self and other, void and profound; Making vows with equality of subject and object;
Prostrating before the reflected manifestations of the Dharma assembly; Practicing the Way by treading upon the true void;
Incense burning to wondrously penetrate non-arising; Reciting the sutras to deeply comprehend the true mark.
Scattering flowers to manifest all non-attachment, snapping fingers to symbolize the removal of dust;

making giving a gateway like an echo in a valley, and cultivating the myriad practices as empty flowers to enter deeply into the ocean of the nature of non-arising, one constantly dwells within the illusory Dharma-gate.
I vow to sever all defiled afflictions; I aspire to be born in the Pure Land of Mind-Only and tread upon the ground of ultimate reality.
Entering and exiting the gates of non-obstructive contemplation, I shall subdue the demonic armies of reflected images and extensively perform Buddha-work within the dream-like world.
Extensively delivering transformed sentient beings, may they together realize the bodhi of quiescent extinction.
*Record of Self-Cultivation* (End). Postscript to the *Record of Self-Cultivation*.
Now, the mind is the fundamental source of all phenomena and the spiritual treasury of wisdom.
It is only because of the deep-seated habits accumulated over kalpas that this wondrous luminosity has been obscured. Consequently, various delusions and falsehoods proliferate incessantly;
thus, life after life one is submerged within saṃsāra, undergoing all manner of bitter suffering, with no constancy in rising or falling—how could this ever come to an end? And when...

Now, the fourfold assembly has turned its merit toward the Buddha Vehicle. Although they rely upon the clear instructions of the Buddhas and Patriarchs to practice the True Dharma as a bridge for transcending the world, their cultivation is slow and their time is wasted;
unable to be courageous and diligent, they fail to swiftly attain Unsurpassed Perfect Enlightenment. Now, I have read the *Self-Record of Practice* by the Patriarch Yongming Yanshou.
In his writings, he recorded the one hundred and eight items of meritorious practice performed each day.

Maintaining both conduct and vows, he benefited himself and others alike, never wasting a single moment of time in vain. Only upon reaching this point did I realize that Master Shou was a returning Buddha from antiquity.

This is not something that we, base and ignorant commoners, dare even to hope for. We have now carved this record, wishing only that our fellow practitioners may arouse a resolute will and open a mind of exceptional discernment;
by no means should you turn back like one gazing at the vast ocean, but rather measure your own strength.
Within this record, one may select one or two passages, or three, five, or ten, and apply oneself with diligence every day as a regular practice.
One must by no means allow a lazy mind to arise, lest one spend time in vain through "one day of heat followed by ten days of frost.

If you can truly act in this way, your efforts will naturally not be in vain; you will gradually enter deeper and deeper, and gradually become broader and more profound, until you reach the Unsurpassed.
Enlightenment (bodhi) is attained unexpectedly; yet, if one does not cultivate actual practice, how could one not fail the resolve made at the time of leaving home?

I humbly pray that this record may circulate throughout the four quarters, so that those who witness it or hear it personally may emulate the diligent cultivation of the ancient worthies, fulfill the aspirations of their entire lives, receive the prediction of enlightenment on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa early, and extensively deliver all beings.
For all sentient beings. This is the colophon.

Written on the day the Buddha attained enlightenment, during the month of Jiaping in the year Gui-mao of the Weida era, by the Bhikṣu Meiyu at the Guxiandi Hermitage in Wulin. Recorded with reverence.
I humbly reflect that during the two successive military calamities of the Gengshen and Xinyou years of the Xianfeng era, my wife, children, and nephews all perished together in the disaster.
When the city of Hangzhou was recaptured in the Jiazi year of the Tongzhi era, I returned to the province from the region of Yue;
my home was as empty as a hanging gourd, I was solitary and alone, and my tears flowed like a spring. I wished to shave my head.
Having entered the Sangha, my transgressions were deeply rooted; driven by necessity, I once again restored the monastic precincts.

In the late autumn of that year, I prostrated myself fully upon the ground and made a vow to do good. Much time has passed since then, and I have repeatedly been protected and sustained by the Buddha’s grace;
thus, my faith has grown even deeper. In the Jiamao year of the Guangxu era, I ascended the mountain to pay homage at Nanshan Jing’ai Temple.

Beside Cisi Temple stood the ancient pagoda of Chan Master Yongming Shou, which had long been neglected and fallen into disrepair. I immediately opened my satchel and provided the funds for its restoration,
reviving the Three Jewels by constructing a mountain gate, two side halls for reciting the Buddha’s name, a guest hall, monastic quarters, and a kitchen.
The kitchen was completed in the year of Gengchen. It began its operations on the Buddha’s Birthday in the fourth month of the year of Jimao.
Every month on the seventeenth day, the Lotus Society and the Lotus Sutra Dharma-assembly were inaugurated to adorn the Pure Land.
While performing prostrations before the stupa and reciting the Buddha’s name, I feared that the distance of the layman’s journey might vary;
thus, I specifically prepared a vegetarian meal as an offering to ease the hardships of his travel. At the end of last year’s winter, I was fortunate enough to receive from Mr.
Xu a copy of the *Xingzhuang* (Record of Conduct) of Chan Master Yongming Youshou. As I humbly read it, I could not contain my joy and peace.
Regarding this work, the original printing blocks were lost during the chaos of war.

I humbly reflect that the Chan Master personally practiced one hundred and eight items [of the *Sūtra of the One Hundred and Eight Meritorious Deeds*], and his merit is immeasurable and boundless. Although my heart aspires to emulate him, I have not yet attained the necessary strength.
Therefore, I shall only provide funds to re-carve the blocks and print copies to distribute throughout the ten directions, so that the great assembly may proclaim them.
I hereby propagate it so that it may circulate widely;
it is my hope that the Buddha-dharma will travel far and wide. This is the humble colophon.
